QUOTE: Set `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... The macros win over any runtime setting... Set only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, leave the macros undefined, and call once during startup... `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is only declared in the runtime configuration. Calling it when the macros are set is a compile error.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter. It also says the setter is not declared when the macros are set, so calling it is a compile error, which makes the two mutually exclusive.
